sections.markdown:
## C — Other important information: what a Class C privilege covers, how to apply, teen permit and practice-hour rules, proof of identity and address, donor, veteran and hearing designations, mandatory insurance minimums and what to do after a collision
Knowledge domain: the vehicles a Class C privilege covers, the age, paperwork, testing and photo requirements to apply, the extra rules for applicants under eighteen, accepted identity and address documents, optional card designations, Oregon's minimum insurance and your duties at a collision; collision reporting, unattended vehicles and loss of privileges continue in part C2.

FACT_ID: sec11-F01 | anchor: A01
A Class C non-commercial driving privilege lets you drive a passenger car, moped, autocycle, van or pickup weighing no more than 26,000 pounds that does not require a commercial driver license or a motorcycle endorsement. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec11-F02 | anchor: A01
You must be at least 15 years old to apply for an instruction permit. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec11-F03 | anchor: A01
You must be at least 16 years old to apply for a driver license. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec11-F04 | anchor: A01
You apply with an electronic application, and an applicant under 18 needs a parent or legal guardian to sign it, or to sign form 735-173DP if that adult cannot come to DMV. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec11-F05 | anchor: A01
An applicant who is emancipated or married shows proof of that status and then needs no parent or guardian signature. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec11-F06 | anchor: A01
Every applicant must present proof of identity, date of birth and residence address. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec11-F07 | anchor: A01
You must provide your Social Security Number or certify electronically that you do not have one. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec11-F08 | anchor: A01
A first-time applicant under 18 needs a parent or guardian to certify school enrollment or attendance, or, if no longer in school, must show a high school diploma or GED certificate. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec11-F09 | anchor: A01
To get the privilege you must pass the required knowledge, vision and drive tests and pay the applicable fees. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec11-F10 | anchor: A01
For the license photo, hats, glasses, face paint or other temporary substances on the face, and contact lenses that change how the eye looks, are not allowed. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec11-F11 | anchor: A01
You cannot be under suspension, revocation or cancellation in Oregon or any other state, and you must surrender any other driving privilege or ID card. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec11-F12 | anchor: A02
An applicant under 18 must have held an instruction permit for at least 6 months before getting a license, and time on an out-of-state permit counts. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0098]

FACT_ID: sec11-F13 | anchor: A02
An applicant under 18 needs 100 hours of supervised driving, or 50 hours plus an ODOT-approved traffic safety education course whose completion proof DMV must receive. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0098]

FACT_ID: sec11-F14 | anchor: A02
Supervised practice counts only when the supervisor is at least 21 years old and has held valid driving privileges for at least 3 years. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0098]

FACT_ID: sec11-F15 | anchor: A02
Documents used as proof of identity and date of birth must be originals or certified copies from the agency that issued them. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0098]

FACT_ID: sec11-F16 | anchor: A02
A U.S. government-issued birth certificate is accepted proof, but hospital-issued birth certificates and baptismal records are not. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0098]

FACT_ID: sec11-F17 | anchor: A02
A U.S. passport or passport card is accepted if it is valid or has been expired no more than 5 years. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0098]

FACT_ID: sec11-F18 | anchor: A02
A DMV-approved tribal ID card from a federally recognized tribe located in Oregon is accepted, as is a Certificate of Naturalization or Certificate of Citizenship. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0098]

FACT_ID: sec11-F19 | anchor: A02
An Employment Authorization Card (I-766), Permanent Resident Card (I-551), foreign passport, Re-entry Permit (I-327) or Refugee Travel Document (I-571) is accepted if valid or expired no more than 5 years. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0098]

FACT_ID: sec11-F20 | anchor: A03
A consulate card is accepted if it is valid or has been expired no more than 5 years. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec11-F21 | anchor: A03
An Oregon driver license, permit or ID card is accepted as proof if valid or expired no more than 13 years. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec11-F22 | anchor: A03
An out-of-state driver license, permit or ID card is accepted as proof only if valid or expired no more than 1 year. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec11-F23 | anchor: A03
If your current legal name differs from the name on your identity document, you must also prove the legal name change. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec11-F24 | anchor: A03
One document is enough to prove your residence address when you apply. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec11-F25 | anchor: A03
Someone who lives at your address can certify it, but that person must come with you and show proof of the address, such as their own license or ID card. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec11-F26 | anchor: A03
Mail from a business, school or government agency showing your first and last name proves your address, but personal mail and forwarded mail do not. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec11-F27 | anchor: A03
A document from an educational provider, a utility hookup order or bill, a mortgage document or a property tax statement can also prove your address. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec11-F28 | anchor: A03
The full list of accepted identity, date of birth, name change and address documents is on OregonDMV.com, and REAL ID requirements are at Oregon.gov/REALID. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec11-F29 | anchor: A04
When you are issued a driving privilege you can join the organ, eye and tissue donor registry, and DMV adds a heart symbol to the front of the card and the words Anatomical Donor to the back. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec11-F30 | anchor: A04
A veteran may ask for a veteran designation by showing a DD214 or DD215 form that shows discharge under honorable conditions. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec11-F31 | anchor: A04
You may ask DMV to add a deaf or hard of hearing designation with no proof required, and it is also visible to law enforcement through your DMV record. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec11-F32 | anchor: A05
Oregon's minimum bodily injury coverage is $25,000 per collision for one person and $50,000 per collision for injury to or death of two or more people. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec11-F33 | anchor: A05
Oregon's minimum property damage coverage is $20,000 per collision for damage to other people's property. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec11-F34 | anchor: A05
Personal Injury Protection must be at least $15,000 per person for reasonable and necessary medical, dental and other expenses incurred within two years after the injury. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec11-F35 | anchor: A05
Uninsured Motorist Coverage must be at least $25,000 per person and $50,000 per collision for bodily injury. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec11-F36 | anchor: A05
The manual calls the word accident misleading: a collision caused by being distracted, tired or not driving defensively is a preventable collision. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec11-F37 | anchor: A05
After a collision you must stop, and if no one is hurt and the vehicles can be moved safely, get them out of the travel lanes quickly and swap information away from the scene. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec11-F38 | anchor: A05
You must give reasonable help to anyone injured in a collision, and injured people should never be moved carelessly. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec11-F39 | anchor: A06
After a collision, give your name, address, driver license number, vehicle plate number and insurance details to the other driver, passengers or any injured pedestrian involved. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec11-F40 | anchor: A06
If anyone is killed or unconscious after a collision, stay at the scene until police arrive. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0102]

Misconceptions: a hospital birth certificate is not accepted proof of birth date; an out-of-state license works as identity proof for a much shorter time after expiry than an Oregon card; personal mail does not prove your address; a police report does not take the place of your own DMV collision report; a crash caused by distraction or fatigue is a preventable collision, not an accident; fifty practice hours are enough only with an approved traffic safety course.
Mnemonics: permit at fifteen, license at sixteen; for teens, six months on a permit and one hundred hours, or half the hours plus a course; supervisor twenty-one with three years licensed; stop, help, swap, stay, report.
Glossary: Class C means the standard non-commercial privilege for cars, vans, pickups, mopeds and autocycles; instruction permit means the learner permit held before a license; Personal Injury Protection means coverage for medical and related costs after a crash; uninsured motorist coverage means coverage when the other driver has no insurance; preventable collision means a crash caused by driver error rather than chance.
Dynamic facts: insurance minimums, document expiry windows, collision report thresholds and fees can change with law and DMV policy, so they are shown as printed in the current manual and re-checked each edition.

corpus_stability.reason: The Oregon Driver Manual is a two-year edition (the front cover names a two-year span and the back cover carries a single form revision code); fees and office details are sent to the DMV website rather than printed, and nothing in the selected pages suggests more than one rewrite per year.
